JAK1: a third domain arrangement, and the experimental structure it matches

Neither open nor closed · produced by OpenFold from wild-type JAK1 sequence with a shallow MSA and no template · Cα cartoon via 3Dmol.js

OpenFold, given the wild-type JAK1 sequence, a shallow MSA and no template, produced a JH2–JH1 arrangement that is neither of the two states the project was looking for. It turns out to be the arrangement seen in 7T6F, the cryo-EM structure of the active JAK1 dimer — a real, measured conformation that was not given to the model in any form.

FERM–JH1 resolves three bands, not two. Closed sits at 40 Å, the third arrangement at 84 Å, open at 92–94 Å. The third state is not a slightly-less-open open state: its SH2–JH1 distance is 52–55 Å against 78 Å for open — JH1 has swung to a different place, not simply moved less far. Note also that JH2–JH1 cannot tell these apart at all (44–48 Å for all three non-closed states), which is why the project stopped selecting structures on it.

Read the first row. Our third arrangement is 4.9 Å from the experimental 7T6F, 47.1 Å from open and 83.0 Å from closed. It is an order of magnitude closer to a measured structure than to either reference state.

And the second cryo-EM structure is a control. 8EWY, also a JAK1 dimer, is 6.3 Å from open and 48.5 Å from 7T6F. So the two experimental JAK1 dimer structures are themselves in different arrangements, and our models reproduce both — the third arrangement matches one, our open models match the other. That is strong evidence the 4.9 Å is a real correspondence and not an artefact of how the metric is defined.

Closed is 80–84 Å from everything else, and the open-family members (8EWY, ma-a1sai, AFDB) agree with each other to 3.4–6.3 Å. The metric is calibrated: same-state pairs land under ~6 Å, different-state pairs above 45 Å. 4.9 Å is same-state.

5. What the arrangement is

From JAK1_third.md, the original analysis:

  • JH1 is rotated ~130–150° relative to the open state (~100–120° relative to closed). It has turned, not just translated.
  • JH1 touches only JH2, through a small interface of its own: JH2 residues ~750 and 798–807, JH1 residues ~930–941 and 997. This interface shares almost nothing with either the open or the closed JH2–JH1 interface, and does not involve the V658 region that is central to the closed interface.
  • It is one arrangement, not a scatter. Six of the seven structures sit within 0.7–9.5 Å of one another; the seventh (64/256 seed 4) is 14–22 Å away and is treated as a variant.
  • The domains are intact. Each domain is within 1.3 Å Cα RMSD of the AF2 model and JH1 pLDDT is 87–91, as high as in the open and closed models. These are not broken or low-confidence structures.

6. Where it appears

MSA depth seeds in the third arrangement
64 / 256all 5 (from recycle ~3–5; seed 4 a variant)
96 / 3842 of 5 (seeds 2 and 4, after recycles 4–7)
128 / 512 and deepernone — open or closed only

No template, 15 recycles, wild-type sequence. The arrangement appears only at shallow MSA depth and disappears as the alignment deepens — the deeper MSA pulls the prediction to the AlphaFold default, which for JAK1 is open.

7. What this is, and what it is not

It is a positive control, not a discovery. 7T6F is a JAK1 structure, so a JAK1 prediction reproducing it shows the pipeline can reach a measured arrangement from sequence alone. It does not show JAK1 is special, and it does not predict anything that was not already known experimentally.

The active-dimer arrangement is JAK1-only in our runs — 35 hits of 129 for JAK1 against 0, 0 and 2 for JAK2, JAK3 and TYK2. Related: JAK2 never reaches an experimentally characterised extended state (0 of 237) even though 96 of its structures match extended AF2 JAK2. In the words of the overnight summary, it "goes extended without going anywhere known".

A correction underlies all of this. 7T6F and 8EWY are mouse JAK1, not JAK2 — 98.0% identity to JAK1_MOUSE against 43.1% to JAK2. An earlier note in this project had them as mouse JAK2, citing P52332, which is itself JAK1_MOUSE. The consequence is substantive and still constrains the rest of the work: there is no experimental multi-domain structure for JAK2, JAK3 or TYK2 at all, so every closed-state number for those three is measured against a prediction or against a cross-paralogue JAK1 structure.
